excerpt: Dograh is an open-source, self-hostable platform for building AI phone agents, pitched as an alternative to Vapi and Retell. Pricing from 1¢ a minute, alternatives and what launch-day users asked.
content:
Dograh is a platform for building voice AI agents that make and answer phone calls: booking appointments, qualifying leads or running payment reminders. You design the call flow in a visual builder, pick your speech-to-text, language model and text-to-speech providers (or a single speech-to-speech model), connect telephony such as Twilio, Plivo, Telnyx or Vonage, and add human transfer, QA and monitoring. You can also build agents from Claude Code, Codex or Cursor through its MCP server.

The whole platform is open source under the BSD 2-Clause licence and can be self-hosted with one command, with your own API keys or local models; the GitHub repository had about 5,900 stars on 14 October 2026. Dograh also runs a hosted cloud. The company behind it is Zansat Technologies Pvt Ltd, an Indian company, according to its terms of service, and its About page lists co-founders Pritesh Kumar and Abhishek Kumar and founding engineer Sabiha Khan.

Dograh launched on Product Hunt on 12 August 2026 and was #1 for the day with 585 points and 205 comments (as of 14 October 2026).

We have not tested Dograh ourselves. This page brings together its official site, its GitHub repository, its Product Hunt page and the public pages of the products it is compared with, and says where each fact comes from.

profile.starts_at: Free to self-host; cloud from 1¢/min platform fee
profile.summary_short: Open-source, self-hostable platform for building AI phone agents, an alternative to Vapi

gallery.alt: Dograh graphic 'Your keys, or Local models' with an AI Models Configuration panel choosing speech-to-text, LLM and text-to-speech providers
Dograh graphic 'Build agents via chat (MCP)' showing Claude Code creating an EMI reminder calling agent through the Dograh MCP server

fit: are a developer or agency building phone agents and want to avoid per-minute platform lock-in
work in a regulated sector or region and need to self-host or deploy on-premises
want to mix providers (Deepgram, Sarvam, ElevenLabs, OpenAI, Gemini and others) or run local models
not_fit: want a ready-made agent with no setup: users on Product Hunt asked for more starter templates
don't want to run servers and need very high call concurrency on the cheapest tier (10 concurrent calls are included)
need a consumer voice assistant rather than a business calling platform

pricing.intro: Dograh lists four options on its own pricing page. Model and telephony costs are separate unless you use Dograh's own models.

plans.name: Open Source
plans.detail: Full platform, self-hosted, no limits, BSD 2-Clause licence

plans.name: Pay as you go
plans.detail: Hosted cloud; bring your own keys or use Dograh Models; 10 concurrent calls included; credits from $5

plans.name: Committed volume
plans.detail: Volume discounts on committed minutes, priority support

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.detail: On-premises or private-cloud deployment, SSO/SAML, audit logs, dedicated account manager and custom SLAs

notes: With your own keys you pay your speech, model and telephony providers directly.

alternatives.intro: These are products Product Hunt lists as alternatives. Review scores are Product Hunt users' own.

items.name: Vapi
items.starts_at: Pay per minute; $5 free credits to start
items.difference: A hosted, closed platform. Dograh positions itself as the open-source alternative you can self-host.

items.name: ElevenLabs
items.what: AI voices, speech and voice agents
items.difference: A voice-model company with its own agent product; Dograh can use ElevenLabs as one of its text-to-speech providers.

items.name: Inworld
items.starts_at: On-demand from $25 per 1M TTS characters; Creator $25/month
items.difference: Supplies voice models; Dograh is the agent-building and telephony layer, and lists Inworld as a provider.

alternatives.more: Product Hunt also lists Deepgram (4.94 from 82 reviews) and SigmaMind AI (4.93 from 14 reviews). Dograh also compares itself with Retell.

quotes.author: Julian Ting
quotes.text: 70+ languages with mid-call switching is a thoughtful feature, especially for real-world phone conversations.

quotes.author: kumar gautam
quotes.text: How is the latency handled for cascaded systems... if one of the api calls fails?
quotes.reply: Abhishek Kumar: TTS and STT run over WebSockets with automatic retries, and fallback LLMs take over if the primary model is slow or fails.

x.none: We did not check X for this profile.

faq.a: An open-source platform for building AI voice agents that make and take phone calls, with a visual flow builder, your choice of speech and language models, telephony, human transfer and monitoring.
The open-source version is free to self-host with no limits. Dograh Cloud charges a platform fee from 1¢ a minute, with credits from $5 (pricing page, 14 October 2026).
Zansat Technologies Pvt Ltd, an Indian company, according to its terms of service. Its About page lists co-founders Pritesh Kumar and Abhishek Kumar.
Its site lists OpenAI, Gemini, Groq, OpenRouter, Azure, AWS, Deepgram, Sarvam, ElevenLabs, Cartesia, Twilio, Plivo, Telnyx, Vonage and others, plus local models.

faq.q: Can I build agents from Claude Code?
faq.a: Yes. Dograh ships an MCP server that works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and other MCP clients.

faq.q: How does Dograh compare with Vapi?
faq.a: Vapi is a hosted platform billed per minute. Dograh offers a similar hosted option but its whole platform is also open source and self-hostable.
